column11: Measured anchor: upadacitinib held 12.1% of US UC patients on advanced therapy in its fourth calendar year after its March 2022 UC approval (Singh S et al., J Crohn's Colitis 2025, as mrk_tulisokibart.csv carries it). Reproduced on this pool (170,408 = 1,253,000 x 0.136; incidence 2,840), the curve (k 1.005, midpoint 2.15) and 27.5% discontinuation, the anchor peak is 0.1009: starts 1,806, 4,211, 8,067 and 11,868 over years 0 to 3, a stock of 20,618, 12.1% of the pool. Multiple 0.5, giving 0.05045, level with tulisokibart's 0.5 (0.05). Evidence for level: Cha and Yu, 'Pharma's first-to-market advantage' (McKinsey, September 2014, 492 launches in 131 classes, 1986 to 2012) find 'a gap between first and second entrant of one year or less is meaningless', and afimkibart starts in 2029, one year after tulisokibart's 2028. Re-solved 2026-10-05 after untreated patients were given an exit (carryover P/(P+I)): the same target now needs 0.0525525, was 0.05045 (the anchor path, now at carryover 0.9836, solves to 0.105105, was 0.100904, times the multiple of 0.5).
column12: the 0.5 multiple is a judgement on that evidence. Case for lower: Roche has no IBD medicine on sale, and the same study finds prior experience in a therapy area nearly doubles an entrant's advantage; the UC market is being taken by the IL-23 antibodies. Case for higher: Roche paid USD 7.1bn upfront for US and Japan rights and puts afimkibart in its '>3bn peak sales' band, unadjusted and for all its indications (HY 2026 results, irp260723.pdf slide 12). pool_crowding rations it with tulisokibart and duvakitug
